newsitem.title: USA: Brent talk fades on crowded US Gulf Coast, for now.
newsitem.headline: Brent talk fades on crowded US Gulf Coast, for now.

text.p: Talk of bringing Brent crude oil from the North Sea to the U.S. Gulf Coast faded on Wednesday, but other foreign crudes were readily available at steadily declining prices, traders said.
Koch Oil, which had previously been showing Brent around May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus 65 cents a barrel, has backed off, traders said.
The Brent talk has dissipated amid increasing speculation over the intentions of British Petroleum, which has accumulated at least 10 April Brent cargoes.
The company was seen as shoring up a strong paper position ahead of possible transatlantic sales next week.
"BP's barrels are expected to come over in a flood next week," a Texas refiner said.

Other North Sea grades were widely available on the Gulf Coast. Statoil was still offering Norwegian Oseberg and Gullfaks around May WTI minus $1.00 and minus 90 cents, respectively, for end-April or early May arrival.
The Norwegian company was also heard offering Heidrun out of Caribbean storage tanks at a discount of around $1.70 a barrel, a level deemed as some 30 cents too pricey by potential buyers.

The May spread between WTI/Cushing and Brent narrowed by around 30 cents to $1.00-05 a barrel Wednesday afternoon, a relatively slim level for transatlantic traffic except for the continued softness of dated Brent.
A dated Brent cargo was sold Wednesday at May Brent minus 97 cents for April 8-10 loading, down three cents from a deal on Tuesday.
West African crude remains plentiful, with Bonny Light and Qua Iboe from Nigeria pegged around WTI minus 40 cents a barrel.
From Latin America, gasoline-rich Cusiana from Colombia was indicated around June WTI minus $1.40-50 a barrel for May 7-11 loading. Bids were seen around $1.70-80 cents discount.
Except for the conspicuous absence of Brent, the Gulf Coast is well-supplied with a variety of foreign crudes, giving buyers an ever-cheaper selection while confounding sellers.
NYMEX crude fell as much as 93 cents over the course of the day on steep technical selling.
